> [!NOTE]
> This repository hosts the **public dashboard** of economic activity in **South Africa** measured with night-time lights seen from space (2014–2025). The site is bilingual (English / French), fully static and regenerated each time the notebook runs.

## 💡 Key messages

1. **National trend** — Between 2014 and 2025, night-time light in South Africa changed by +1.4% per year (95% CI: -0.0% to +2.3%). Over the last 12 months, the seasonally adjusted level is +4.0% relative to the previous 12 months.  
   <sub>🟠 medium · trend significant at the 10% level (p = 0.06)</sub>
2. **Regions** — Of 52 ADM2 units, 31 show significant growth, 17 are stagnating and 4 are declining. Light remains concentrated: Gauteng accounts for 24% of national light.  
   <sub>🟠 medium · classification of 52 units, threshold ±1%/yr and p < 0.10</sub>
3. **Convergence** — Across ADM2 units, light per capita converges: the least-lit units are catching up.  
   <sub>🟠 medium · β = −0.074 [−0.092; −0.056], n = 52</sub>
4. **Link with GDP** — The elasticity of light with respect to real GDP is 1.34 in levels (95% CI: −0.54 to 3.21, R² = 0.28, 12 years) and −0.04 in growth rates (CI: −0.62 to 0.54). In pseudo-real time (each year predicted from earlier years only), light growth tracks GDP growth with a correlation of −0.67 (mean absolute error: 2.7 percentage points of growth, no better than the best naive forecast, error ratio 1.11).  
   <sub>🔴 low · n = 12, not significant (p = 0.16)</sub>
5. **Shocks** — The most pronounced shock in the seasonally adjusted series is “COVID-19”: trough of -13.1% (09/2020), return to the pre-shock level after 8 months.  
   <sub>🟠 medium · trough compared with pre-shock month-to-month variability</sub>
6. **Inequality and access** — The Gini coefficient of light per capita (ADM2) is 0.16 in 2025 (no significant change since 2014). About 2.84 million people live in inhabited areas with no detectable light (5% of the inhabited population).  
   <sub>🟠 medium · sensitive to the radiance threshold (from 0.00 to 5.62 M depending on the threshold); a proxy for outdoor lighting, not for grid connection</sub>

## ⚙️ How it is computed

Processing chain run on Google Earth Engine from the *Night-time lights and economic activity* notebook (part 3):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["🛰️ VIIRS DNB monthly<br/>and annual (VNL V2)"] --> B["🧹 Cleaning<br/>clouds · gas flares · background"]
    B --> C["🗺️ Zonal statistics<br/>country · regions · districts"]
    P["👥 GHSL population<br/>🏭 non-residential built-up<br/>💨 Sentinel-5P NO₂"] --> C
    C --> D["📈 Series, trends,<br/>shocks, breaks"]
    C --> E["⚖️ Inequality,<br/>people in the dark"]
    C --> F["🏭 Industrial zones"]
    W["🏦 World Bank<br/>GDP · electricity access"] --> G["💹 Light–GDP<br/>elasticity"]
    C --> G
    D & E & F & G --> H["🌍 Bilingual dashboard<br/>GitHub Pages"]
    classDef default fill:#E8F5EF,stroke:#00704A,color:#231F20;
    class H fill:#00704A,color:#fff,stroke:#F5C242
```

<details>
<summary><b>The six analyses in detail</b></summary>


| | |
|---|---|
| **📈 Time dynamics** | STL decomposition, year-on-year change, Theil–Sen trend with Mann–Kendall test, anomalies, breaks |
| **🗺️ Regional growth** | Growth / Stagnation / Decline classes (Benjamini–Hochberg correction), HHI, β and σ convergence |
| **💹 Lights and GDP** | elasticity (HAC errors, bootstrap), nowcast judged against two naive forecasts, experimental regional GDP |
| **⚡ Shocks** | trough, gap vs trend, months to recovery, placebo test, Black Marble daily index |
| **⚖️ Inequality and access** | Gini, Theil (between / within regions), urban / rural ratio, people in the dark at three thresholds |
| **🏭 Industrial zones** | four-signal score (light, non-residential built-up, low density, NO₂), OpenStreetMap validation |

</details>

## ⚠️ Limitations to keep in mind

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Lights measure radiance at about 1:30 a.m., not value added. Keep in mind:
>
> - **Blooming and saturation** — light spills beyond built-up areas; the brightest cores plateau
> - **Gas flares** — bright without local activity: masked, but worth watching
> - **Seasonality** — clouds, fires and vegetation create non-economic cycles
> - **Sensor breaks** — DMSP → VIIRS, VNL V2.1 → V2.2: handled with dummies, not eliminated
> - **Rural areas** — the signal is weakest where the rural poor live
> - **Status** — experimental estimates, not official statistics

## 🔁 Reproduce or adapt to another country

The site is produced by the **Night-time lights and economic activity** notebook (part 3) (Colab). Changing the `ISO3` code in the parameters cell is enough to analyse another country; sections 12 and 13 export and re-publish this repository.
